summary:
# NOTES: THE GATELESS BARRIER (Lucas Malet, 1900, Dodd, Mead & Co.)

Single book, no BOOK headings. Chapters I–XXV.

## Front matter
- Preface: quote from Lafcadio Hearn (*Exotics and Retrospectives*, pp. 83-84). Mu-Mon-Kwan ("The Gateless Barrier"), a Zen/Dhyana text, not explanatory; questions posed, student must think answers out, not write them. Story "supposed to be true" but used only as a Dhyana question.

## Characters
- **Laurence Rivers**: protagonist, Englishman, about 31 (“just over thirty”; “thirty-one years”), sailor/sportsman (golf, polo, rackets, yachting), minor poet/playwright (his little comedy, verses), married ~2 years to Virginia. Kind, genial, vain, restless; "kept the best of himself to himself."
- **Virginia Rivers** (née Van Reenan family, American, New York/Newport "smart set"): his wife, bright, clever, fashionable, self-satisfied; "modern, mundane." Says "Why should she worry... everybody was always crossing now." Wants no children yet ("spare the fair Virginias"). Sends telegram "Wanted here immediately. Return next steamer. Virginia." Resembles Botticelli Madonna. Clear-eyed, obstinate, unemotional.
- **Mr. Montagu Rivers** (uncle, elder Mr. Rivers): morose, eccentric, misogynist, materialist/rationalist, collector, studied physics, philology, metaphysics. Gaunt, transparent, blue-grey eyes, violet dressing-gown, violet velvet skull-cap. Two rings (amethyst with Arabic characters; black scarab on gold hoop). Crystal memento mori (rock crystal skull, jade olive crown). Dies in bed (ebony bed with sphinxes and caryatides, Medusa carving). Dies after Laurence's visit; body found hanging from bed. Had a secret: witnessed supernatural manifestations in the yellow drawing-room, denied them, "miserably and grossly" failed. Says "gateless barrier" line: "Reason, learning, the senses... project us against a gateless barrier at the last!"
- **Agnes Rivers**: ghost/revenant; cousin of Dudley; fiancée of Laurence Rivers (namesake, 1st Laurence, naval lieutenant, Trafalgar). Pale rose-red silk gown, muslin/lace cape, pearls, diamond-powdered slippers, dark hair, blue-purple eyes. Dies of grief ~1805 (buried in Stoke Rivers vault; coffin found empty except lead coffin plate...). Was 21 at engagement; wrote letters 1802-1805; guardian Dudley. Speaks only once Laurence speaks; wordless at first.
- **Dudley Rivers**: Laurence's (first) elder brother, atheist/radical, friend of Robespierre, travelled France; guardian of Agnes; tall, thin, long pale hair, fanatical eyes; died; body in vault. Opposed the match.
- **Laurence Rivers (1st, namesake, great-uncle)**: younger brother of Dudley; naval lieutenant; shot through lungs at Trafalgar; miniature by Cosway at 21, dark-blue naval uniform, queue. Engraved on watch "L. R."; gift inscription "Laurence, a gift to his dear love," Aug 1803; "Agnes, a gift to her dear cousin."
- **Denbigh Rivers**: Laurence's father, died in Malta on foreign service.
- **Mrs. Lambart (Mrs. Lambert)**: Agnes's chaperone/companion.
- **Mr. Burkinshaw**: rector c.1803, preached to Agnes.
- **Renshaw**: butler (egg-shaped face, large, respectful).
- **Watkins**: under-butler, portly, soft hands.
- **Lowndes**: valet, long-armed, wiry, grey-haired/grey-faced; 40 years service.
- **Armstrong**: agent, Scottish, ~60, kite-shaped face, "Aweel," Presbyterian; grandfather was factor to Dudley; Cupar/Fife connection; three generations.
- **Mr. Wormald**: family solicitor, small, withered, squirrel-eyed, gouty hands.
- **Walter Samuel Beal**: curate-in-charge at Stoke Rivers; mild, sandy hair, spectacles, moist white hands; fears supernatural; "Scarlet Woman" in red dress seen at window; fell over strings at school (hoax).
- **Archdeacon** (of Bishop's Pudbury): rector-archdeacon; levelled churchyard there; read burial service.
- **Mr. Wingate**: rector of Stoke Rivers (absent, at Cheltenham).
- **Captain Jack Bellingham**: army, fair, gossipy, ~35; wife **Louise (Mrs. Bellingham)**, cousin of Virginia (née Van Reenan); children Sibyl (girl, scarlet jacket), younger girl, three-year-old son; live at Bishop's Pudbury manor-house; Mrs B. "spook-hunting," psychical research.
- **Horace Greener**: young society man, Newport/NY; Laurence's golf partner.
- **Doctor (eminent London surgeon)**: courtly, amateur of art, examined body.
- **Willie Van Reenan**: theatricals.
- **Padre Sahib** nickname for Beal.

## Places
- **Stoke Rivers**, Sussex, Courthouse/house shaped as reversed L; main building on south front; dark oak panelling, dark blue damask; electric light; hot-air ventilation at ~70°F; oppressive; Italian garden (cypresses, white statues, fountains, golden gravel walk, lime-tree avenue, stone bench); corridor of Roman emperor busts (Augustus, Tiberius, Nero, two Antonines, Caligula, Commodus); tapestry curtain (satyr and naked woman driven by cupids), leather-lined, hides door to **yellow drawing-room** (satin-wood furniture, Boucher-style paintings, Sèvres jars, Empire clock with garnets, Chelsea figures, harp, tambour frame, work-box with thimble, Dante *Vita Nuova*, St Francis de Sales *Introduction to the Devout Life*, violin in red velvet case, piano, escritoire with locks/13 keys, Cosway miniatures).
- Stoke Rivers churchyard: small Norman church, yew trees, Rivers vault; rectory ¾ mile across valley.
- **Bishop's Pudbury**: 8 miles away; Bellinghams' house (manor reconstructed).
- Turnpike house at crossroads on high table-land; view of sea, Beachy Head, Downs; phantom Indiamen and frigates.
- **Hazledown gypsum quarries**; light railway project.
- Virginia's summer house: American, Atlantic coast, Van Reenan property, river, New England woods.
- Ship crossing Atlantic (March); Cuyp, Ruysdael, Nicholas Poussin paintings.

## Events in order
1. Ch. I: On ship, March night, Laurence (married ~2 yrs) feels freedom; recalls uncle's letter (misogynist, "pearls before swine"). Summoned by uncle's illness (Mr. Wormald). Virginia not invited. Quote: "What shall it profit a man... if he gain the whole world and lose his own soul?"
2. Ch. II: Meets uncle. Uncle explains he wants to study Laurence as "the average man"/Commonplace ("dropped an important link out of the chain of being"). Denies affection. "Be yourself... Be passive." Laurence agrees. Rings chink. Crystal skull.
3. Ch. III: Tours house; hot, enervating; corridor; passes tapestry; door behind it; finds yellow drawing-room with harp, work-box, Dante; touches thimble, plays violin; "playing the fool." Sees hunt (cry of hounds). Strolls to stables.
4. Ch. IV: Drives to Bishop's Pudbury to leave Virginia's gifts for Bellingham daughter; Mrs B. out. Returns to dinner; letter from Beal (curate, "Padre Sahib") begging admittance to uncle; Laurence amused.
5. Ch. V: Dinner conversation with uncle about woman; uncle: "subject of sex... distasteful." Laurence defends love, "We shall have degeneration" if women only for breeding. Uncle: "Your wife—"; Laurence: "My wife does not enter into our contract." Laurence returns; passes tapestry again; re-enters yellow drawing-room; sees rose-pink-gowned woman at escritoire.
6. Ch. VI: Woman searches for something; Laurence asks, "what have you lost?" She turns, pale, beautiful face (blue-purple eyes). Laurence recalls Virginia and other flames. She goes away behind escritoire.
7. Ch. VII: Restless night; rationalizes dream; dawn; "Poor dear Virginia!" Morning: visits churchyard, considers burial plot; Norman church, yews, rooks. Ambition stirs.
8. Ch. VIII: Visits Beal at rectory (dining-room); Beal's churchyard-levelling story; Beal's hoax at choir practice (strings across door, fell in mud); Beal fears house after dark, "female in the house," "Scarlet Woman," saw a person in red dress at bow window. Laurence invites Beal to dine; Beal refuses. Laurence returns to yellow room: empty.
9. Ch. IX: Captain Bellingham calls, gossip; wants Laurence's wife's cult; Louise wants "spook" story. Laurence visits uncle: uncle refuses to discuss supernatural, then confesses: "I cannot deny the existence of supernatural manifestations... in one quarter of this house." Says he lied to his reason; "gateless barrier" not yet. Laurence promises to keep results secret, only report to uncle. Laurence goes to the yellow room: woman; he pleads for her; she awakens, smiles; they walk Italian garden, lime avenue, stone bench; he talks of his life; she vanishes at dawn after train passes and cocks crow.
10. Ch. XI: Wakes late; Watkins; Virginia's letter. Laurence rides, passes churchyard, decides to buy burial plot. Lunch with Louise Bellingham at Pudbury; she probes "family spectre"; Laurence annoyed; children with balloons; Laurence reflects on Commonplace, decides to retire to it, then flags. Vision of East Indiamen and frigates from turnpike; Stoke Rivers in strange light.
11. Ch. XII: Uncle talks until midnight (Chaldean cylinders, Gnosticism, Averroes).
12. Ch. XIII: Laurence opens escritoire (13th key). Finds packets of letters 1802-05, relics (buckles, shells, coral charm, posies, Trafalgar? no—watch with L.R.). Two Cosway miniatures: Agnes and Laurence (1st). Reads letters (Agnes to Laurence: Dudley's opposition, Mrs Lambert, Burkinshaw; final letter: "In six months I shall attain my majority"; ends in blood-stains).
13. Ch. XIV: Renshaw: uncle won't receive. Laurence with Armstrong (agent) in library; Armstrong tells family history: Dudley an atheist; Laurence (1st) died at Trafalgar; Agnes "died" of grief; coffin reportedly filled with rubbish; "as the poet says..."
14. Ch. XV: Laurence resolves to lift the veil; jealous; goes to yellow room; struggles with unseen force; nothingness terror; Renshaw and Watkins summon: uncle "very ill."
15. Ch. XVI: Uncle dying: speech on matter, spirit, "love is the language of spirit"; "gateless barrier"; uncle: "The barrier needs must remain gateless" (for him). Uncle dies, hanging out of bed.
16. Ch. XVII: Funeral preparations: vault opened at Stoke Rivers church; Dudley's and Denbigh's coffins; Agnes's coffin not found. Laurence asks Armstrong about plot near chancel wall. Wormald arrives. Laurence sleeps in yellow room, dreams of Agnes at lime-trees; Trafalgar vision; "Agnes, Agnes" / "Laurence, Laurence."
17. Ch. XVIII: Conversation with Agnes (speech restored, "I have always known that you would come again"). They talk till dawn. She vanishes.
18. Ch. XIX: Uncle's will: servants paid; Laurence inherits. Clause requiring surgeon verification of death. Surgeon examines, admires collection; Laurence declines to reveal secret. Laurence keeps vigil with Lowndes over corpse; resolves to take his own course.
19. Ch. XX: Funeral. Archdeacon present. Bellinghams; Virginia "the Archdeacon." Laurence and Agnes in garden; she asks if Dudley is dead; Laurence, jealous, presses. Agnes sings. Dawn: a faint shadow follows her.
20. Ch. XXI: Summer: Laurence stays, recluse, fasts, ascetic; estate work (light railway to Hazledown); Agnes more solid. Morning talk at bay window: "The day does not belong to me yet." He plans sacramental feast (bread and wine) to restore her body.
21. Ch. XXII: Returns home from work; telegram from Virginia; decides to repudiate Virginia; orders uncut loaf of bread and fruit/wine.
22. Ch. XXIII: Agnes at piano (minuet); he takes her hands—warm and living; carries her across threshold (curtain); dining room feast; she sneezes; refuses bread, then eats, realizes "to eat is sin"; she refuses his demands; calls his claim "the call"; she leaves, "Go back to the world... I will go back too... There I shall await your coming... being one with Almighty and Eternal God." Vanishes. Storm over; stars.
23. Ch. XXIV: Virginia's verandah party, Van Reenan summer (New England, river); Horace Greener; Laurence reads letters: Armstrong's packet; Beal's letter: coffin charred at corner, second lead coffin with inscription legible; Beal says the Archdeacon read service; Agnes's coffin "provisionally" placed in reserved plot. Laurence: "She saved me from committing a great sin." Virginia: "Are you aware that you become very indelicate?" Laurence says he'll return in two weeks. Fire at Stoke Rivers (electric wire, panelling) burned the yellow room.
24. Ch. XXV: August; Laurence returns; Renshaw and Lowndes welcome; burned room; candles; vault chamber with Agnes's coffin found beneath the escritoire; vigil; procession of clouds; dawn at churchyard; new grave with osier cage and pink wild-rose crown; John 3:8 "The wind bloweth where it listeth." Laurence's resolve: work, no woman harmed. Epilogue: Virginia rebuilt yellow room, Laurence keeps it for himself; Laurence went south to war; Jack Bellingham volunteered. Final: "THE END."

## Key quotes
- "What shall it profit a man..."
- "gateless barrier"
- "Laurence, Laurence" / "Agnes, Agnes"
- "a gift to his dear love"
- "I cannot deny the existence of supernatural manifestations."
- "Wanted here immediately. Return next steamer. Virginia."
- "after all, dear love, we go forth together,--amen."

## Other
- Books listed: Vita Nuova, Introduction to the Devout Life; Times newspaper; Dante/Boucher references; Omar? no.
- Dates: March (arrival); August 1803 (miniatures); Trafalgar (21 Oct 1805, unstated date, "three months" before wedding).
- Numbers: 13 keys (the 13th opens escritoire); 70°F; 8 miles to Pudbury; ¾ mile to rectory; Virginia's 2 years marriage; Laurence 31.
